title: Awesome Grade Calculator
description: A gamified project evaluation system with MOBA-style ranking progression.

caseStudy.problem: Grade tracking tools are boring and students disengage quickly. I wanted to make checking scores feel more like leveling up in a game.
caseStudy.approach: Mapped letter grades to MOBA-style rank tiers (Bronze → Challenger). Built a clean input form with real-time rank display and animated rank-up transitions using vanilla JS and CSS animations.
caseStudy.learned: That gamification is really just good UX — feedback loops, clear progress, and emotional payoff. Also learned to keep DOM updates efficient by only touching changed elements.

title: PX-to-REM Converter
description: A polished interactive converter with batch processing.

caseStudy.problem: Manually converting px to rem while writing CSS is tedious and error-prone. Existing tools online are cluttered with ads or require too many clicks.
caseStudy.approach: Built a single-focus tool: paste a list of px values, get rem values instantly. Supports custom base font size and batch conversion in one text area.
caseStudy.learned: The value of building for yourself first. When the user is also the developer, you naturally cut every unnecessary feature and focus on speed.

title: EXXEED | The Mission Log
description: Serverless blogging platform built on Cloudflare Workers.

caseStudy.problem: I wanted a personal blog with zero hosting cost, no CMS overhead, and full ownership of the stack — something that runs at the edge globally.
caseStudy.approach: Built entirely on Cloudflare Workers with KV storage for posts. No database, no server — just edge functions and key-value pairs. Custom admin UI for writing and publishing.
caseStudy.learned: Serverless architecture forces you to think differently about state, latency, and data shape. KV's eventual consistency made me rethink how I structure writes vs. reads.

title: Oldagram
description: Instagram clone with dynamic feed rendering.

caseStudy.problem: The Scrimba challenge was to replicate Instagram's core feed UI from a static mockup — a great test of translating design to code precisely.
caseStudy.approach: Rendered a dynamic feed from a JS data array, matching the mockup's layout with CSS Flexbox. Added like-toggle interactivity and a hover detail panel.
caseStudy.learned: How to go from a design spec to a working component without a framework. Reinforced that good HTML structure makes CSS 10x easier to write.
